answer.origin: NVIDIA Corporation company blog statement, dated 2026-07-01 (incoming).
answer.note: NVIDIA says it is introducing a model under which AI clouds can procure NVIDIA infrastructure with revenue sharing and credit support; the clouds sell NVIDIA-powered services, while NVIDIA earns standard product revenue plus a share of cloud revenue on supported capacity (incoming). This is a company-described commercial model, not evidence that the stated revenue stream has already been realized. If partnerships use the model and supported capacity is deployed and utilized, it could add usage-linked revenue alongside product sales; the source does not quantify the effect. NVIDIA says AI cloud companies are building DSX AI factories (item:e3). It specifically says Firmus is building a Batam campus expected to scale to 360 MW and up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs (item:e4), a potential deployment and infrastructure-demand signal, not a disclosed order or proof that Firmus directly procures that equipment from NVIDIA. Sharon AI’s CEO describes a strategic collaboration on sovereign, large-scale AI compute infrastructure (item:e2), but gives no commercial terms. NVIDIA also names Baseten, Fireworks AI and Together AI as examples of AI-native demand; this supports the relevance of the demand theme, not a claim that they are customers or have committed purchases.
limitations: The source does not specify which AI clouds participate in the revenue-sharing and credit-support model, the terms or extent of credit support, the revenue-share basis, or the amount of capacity covered.
It does not report realized revenue, utilization, deployment timing, or the model’s financial contribution to NVIDIA.

For Firmus, the stated 360 MW and up to 170,000 GPUs are expected scale, not a reported completed deployment; the source gives no schedule, financing details, purchase commitment, or direct supplier relationship for that campus.
The Sharon AI quotation identifies a collaboration but does not establish its scope, commercial terms, or implementation status.
follow_up: Check subsequent NVIDIA filings and company announcements for named AI-cloud participants, executed commercial arrangements, credit-support exposure, and any disclosed revenue-sharing terms.
Track NVIDIA filings and earnings commentary for reported deployment, utilization, and revenue attributable to supported AI-cloud capacity.
Check Firmus announcements and filings for campus financing, construction and deployment milestones, GPU procurement commitments, and the identity of equipment suppliers.
Seek details from Sharon AI or NVIDIA on the collaboration’s scope and implementation.
